# PitchBook Python API Docs | dltHub

Build a PitchBook-to-database pipeline in Python using dlt with AI harness support for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.

Last updated: Nov 20, 2026

PitchBook is a market intelligence platform providing a RESTful API for on-demand access to private and public market data such as companies, deals, investors, and funds. The REST API base URL is `https://api.pitchbook.com` and all requests require an Authorization header with a custom token format.

dlt is an open-source Python library that handles authentication, pagination, and schema evolution automatically. dlthub provides AI context files that enable code assistants to generate production-ready pipelines. Install with `uv add "dlt[hub]"` and start loading PitchBook data in under 10 minutes.

---

##

Here are some of the endpoints you can load from PitchBook:

| Resource | Endpoint | Method | Data selector | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| companies | companies/search | GET | | Search companies using query parameters |
| deals | deals/search | GET | | Search deals using query parameters |
| people | people/search | GET | | Search people using query parameters |
| investors | investors/{id} | GET | | Get investor by id |
| funds | funds/{id} | GET | | Get fund by id |

---

## How do I authenticate with the PitchBook API?

PitchBook authenticates requests using a static API key passed in the Authorization header with the format 'PB-Token {API_KEY}'.

**1. Get your credentials**

Access to the PitchBook API is a paid, contract-gated add-on and is not available via a self-serve dashboard. To obtain credentials: 1. Contact your PitchBook account manager or your organization's PitchBook administrator to request API access. 2. Once the add-on is enabled, your account manager will provision your API key. 3. Alternatively, you can log in to the PitchBook platform and navigate to 'My PitchBook' > 'Plugins & Apps' > 'PitchBook API' to reach out to the Direct Data team to initiate the request.

**2. Add them to `.dlt/secrets.toml`**

```
[sources.pitchbook_source]
api_key = "your_pb_token_here"
```

dlt reads this automatically at runtime — never hardcode tokens in your pipeline script. For production environments, see [setting up credentials with dlt](https://dlthub.com/docs/walkthroughs/add_credentials) for environment variable and vault-based options.

---

## How do I set up and run the pipeline?

**Set up a virtual environment and install dlt:**

```
uv init
uv add "dlt[hub]"
```

**1. Install the `dlt` AI harness:**

```
uv run dlthub ai init --agent <your-agent> # <agent>: claude | cursor | codex
```

This installs project rules, a secrets management skill, appropriate ignore files, and configures the `dlt` MCP server for your agent. [Learn more →](https://dlthub.com/docs/dlt-ecosystem/llm-tooling/llm-native-workflow)

**2. Install the `rest-api-pipeline` toolkit:**

```
uv run dlthub ai toolkit install rest-api-pipeline
```

This loads the skills and context about `dlt` the agent uses to build the pipeline iteratively, efficiently, and safely. The agent uses MCP tools to inspect credentials — it never needs to read your `secrets.toml` directly. [Learn more →](https://dlthub.com/docs/dlt-ecosystem/llm-tooling/llm-native-workflow#anatomy-of-the-toolkit)

**3. Start LLM-assisted coding:**

```
Use /find-source to load data from the PitchBook API into DuckDB.
```

The **`rest-api-pipeline`** toolkit takes over from here — it reads relevant API documentation, presents you with options for which endpoints to load, and follows a structured workflow to scaffold, debug, and validate the pipeline step by step.

**4. Run the pipeline:**

```
uv run python pitchbook_pipeline.py
```

If everything is configured correctly, you'll see output like this:

```
Pipeline pitchbook_pipeline load step completed in 0.26 seconds
1 load package(s) were loaded to destination duckdb and into dataset pitchbook_data
The duckdb destination used duckdb:/pitchbook.duckdb location to store data
Load package 1749667187.541553 is LOADED and contains no failed jobs
```

**Inspect your pipeline and data:**

```
uv run dlthub show
```

This opens the Pipeline Dashboard where you can verify pipeline state, load metrics, schema (tables, columns, types), and query the loaded data directly.

---

## Python pipeline example

This example loads Because the PitchBook API is highly customized based on the specific data points requested by an organization, common endpoints depend on your specific contract. Typically, developers interact with companies and deals endpoints to pull market data. from the PitchBook API into DuckDB. It mirrors the endpoint and data selector configuration from the table above:

```
import dlt
from dlt.sources.rest_api import RESTAPIConfig, rest_api_resources

@dlt.source
def pitchbook_source(api_key=dlt.secrets.value):
    config: RESTAPIConfig = {
        "client": {
            "base_url": "https://api.pitchbook.com",
            "auth": {"type": "api_key", "api_key": api_key, "name": "Authorization", "location": "header"},
        },
        "resources": [
            {"name": "companies", "endpoint": {"path": "companies/search"}},
            {"name": "deals", "endpoint": {"path": "deals/search"}}
        ],
    }
    yield from rest_api_resources(config)


def get_data() -> None:
    pipeline = dlt.pipeline(
        pipeline_name="pitchbook_pipeline",
        destination="duckdb",
        dataset_name="pitchbook_data",
    )
    load_info = pipeline.run(pitchbook_source())
    print(load_info)
```

To add more endpoints, append entries from the resource table to the `"resources"` list using the same `name`, `path`, and `data_selector` pattern.

---

## How do I query the loaded data?

Once the pipeline runs, dlt creates one table per resource. You can query with Python or SQL.

**Python (pandas DataFrame):**

```
import dlt

data = dlt.pipeline("pitchbook_pipeline").dataset()
sessions_df = data.companies.df()
print(sessions_df.head())
```

**SQL (DuckDB example):**

```
SELECT * FROM pitchbook_data.companies LIMIT 10;
```

**In a marimo or Jupyter notebook:**

```
import dlt

data = dlt.pipeline("pitchbook_pipeline").dataset()
data.companies.df().head()
```

See [how to explore your data in marimo Notebooks](https://dlthub.com/docs/general-usage/dataset-access/marimo) and [how to query your data in Python with dataset](https://dlthub.com/docs/general-usage/dataset-access/dataset).

---

##

dlt supports loading into any of these destinations — only the `destination` parameter changes:

| Destination | Example value |
|---|---|
| DuckDB (local, default) | `"duckdb"` |
| PostgreSQL | `"postgres"` |
| BigQuery | `"bigquery"` |
| Snowflake | `"snowflake"` |
| Redshift | `"redshift"` |
| Databricks | `"databricks"` |
| Filesystem (S3, GCS, Azure) | `"filesystem"` |

Change the destination in `dlt.pipeline(destination="snowflake")` and add credentials in `.dlt/secrets.toml`. See the [full destinations list](https://dlthub.com/docs/dlt-ecosystem/destinations/).
